cards.text: Friend, meet Hezekiah, king of Judah. The LORD has saved him and Jerusalem from the king of Assyria, and now all the nations look up to him. Then, in those days, Hezekiah becomes mortally ill.

cards.question: Hezekiah, king of Judah, is mortally ill. What does he do?
When Hezekiah prays, the LORD speaks to him and gives him a sign.

cards.text: That's favor from the LORD, friend. When I got pulled out of that junk drawer, I said thank you so many times my OVENS started saying "you're welcome" back. But Hezekiah doesn't repay the favor shown to him.

cards.question: Hezekiah doesn't repay the favor the LORD showed him. Why not?

answers.text: His advisers talk him out of it

cards.question: Because Hezekiah's heart is proud, wrath comes upon him and upon Judah and ___.
With wrath on him and his people, Hezekiah ___ the pride of his heart.
Hezekiah humbles himself all alone, while the people of Jerusalem stay proud.
Because Hezekiah and the people humble themselves, the wrath of the LORD doesn't come upon them during the days of ___.

cards.text: Hezekiah has very great riches and honor, with treasuries and storehouses to hold it all, because God gave him very great wealth. Meanwhile I owned ONE handle with my name carved in it, and I thought I was LIVING.
Hezekiah's a builder too. At the Spring of Gihon, he blocks the upper outlet and sends that water somewhere new.

cards.question: Hezekiah blocks the upper outlet of the Spring of Gihon and channels the water down to the ___ side of the City of David.

cards.text: Hezekiah prospers in all he does. Then visitors show up: ambassadors sent by the rulers of Babylon.

cards.question: Ambassadors from the rulers of Babylon come to Hezekiah. What do they want to ask about?

answers.text: The wonder that happened in the land

cards.question: While the ambassadors from Babylon are there, God leaves Hezekiah alone to test him, so He might know all that is in Hezekiah's heart.

cards.text: The rest of Hezekiah's acts and his deeds of loving devotion are written in the vision of the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz, in the Book of the Kings of Judah and Israel. My whole life story? Five letters carved in a handle. D-O-R-I-N. That's it. That's the WHOLE book.

cards.question: Hezekiah rests with his fathers. Where is he buried?

answers.text: In the upper tombs of David's descendants
In the garden of his own palace
In the cave of Machpelah at Hebron

cards.question: At Hezekiah's death, all Judah and the people of Jerusalem pay him honor.
After Hezekiah dies, his son ___ reigns in his place.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the statement about the LORD's favor, the junk-drawer joke, and the statement that Hezekiah does not repay the favor.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The setup says only that Hezekiah sends the water somewhere new. Nothing in the earlier cards lets the baker reason out west rather than east or north, so this blank tests an unseen detail by guessing.
